# Homescape Construction Inc. — Complete Reference

> Licensed Chicago general contractor specializing in residential remodeling and custom home building since 2012. Owner-operated with 200+ completed projects and 98% client satisfaction.

## About Homescape Construction

Homescape Construction Inc. is a Chicago-based residential construction company founded in 2012. As an owner-operated business, Homescape provides hands-on project management for every job, from initial consultation through final walkthrough. The company has completed over 200 residential projects across Chicago's North Side, Northwest Side, and nearby suburbs. Homescape maintains a 98% client satisfaction rate and holds a 4.9-star average rating across more than 200 verified reviews on platforms including Houzz, Google, and the Better Business Bureau. The company is a licensed general contractor in Illinois, fully insured and bonded for residential construction work.

## Service Details

### Kitchen Remodeling in Chicago

Kitchen remodeling is one of the most impactful home improvement projects for Chicago homeowners. A typical mid-range kitchen remodel in Chicago costs between $35,000 and $75,000, according to 2024-2025 market data. This investment typically includes new cabinetry, countertops (granite, quartz, or butcher block), flooring, lighting fixtures, plumbing fixtures, and professional installation labor. High-end kitchen renovations featuring custom cabinetry, premium appliances, and designer finishes can exceed $100,000. The average kitchen remodel timeline in Chicago runs 8-12 weeks from demolition to completion, with permit approval adding 2-4 weeks upfront. Most Chicago kitchen remodels require permits from the Chicago Department of Buildings, particularly for electrical and plumbing modifications.

### Bathroom Remodeling in Chicago

Bathroom remodeling projects in Chicago typically range from $15,000 to $40,000 for a full renovation. This includes custom tile work, new shower or tub installation, vanity replacement, plumbing updates, and lighting improvements. Homescape specializes in both primary bathroom renovations and powder room updates. Accessibility upgrades—including grab bars, curbless showers, and ADA-compliant fixtures—are increasingly requested by Chicago homeowners planning to age in place. A standard bathroom remodel takes 4-6 weeks to complete. Chicago building permits are required for bathroom renovations involving plumbing relocation or electrical work.

### Basement Finishing in Chicago

Basement finishing transforms unused square footage into functional living space. In Chicago, basement finishing typically costs $25,000 to $60,000 depending on size and amenities. A finished basement can add a bedroom, home office, entertainment room, or rental unit to a Chicago home. Key considerations for Chicago basements include waterproofing (essential given the clay soil and high water table), proper egress windows for bedrooms, and HVAC integration. Chicago requires permits for basement finishing projects, including inspections for framing, electrical, plumbing, and final occupancy. Average project duration is 6-10 weeks after permit approval.

### Home Additions in Chicago

Home additions in Chicago cost approximately $150 to $300 per square foot, varying by complexity and finish level. Common addition types include single-room additions, second-story additions, and bump-outs. Second-story additions in Chicago require structural engineering to assess foundation capacity and typically cost more than ground-level additions. Chicago zoning regulations, including lot coverage and setback requirements, significantly impact addition feasibility. The permit process for additions involves architectural drawings, structural plans, and multiple inspections. Timeline for a typical addition: 4-8 months from design through completion.

### ADU and Coach House Construction in Chicago

Accessory dwelling units (ADUs) became legal citywide in Chicago with the 2020 ADU ordinance, effective 2021. Chicago now permits ADUs on most residential lots, including garage conversions, coach houses, and basement apartments. ADU construction costs in Chicago range from $150,000 to $350,000 depending on size, design, and site conditions. Chicago ADU requirements include a minimum lot size, owner-occupancy requirement (either main house or ADU), and parking considerations in some zones. Coach houses—detached ADUs above garages—are popular in Chicago's North Side neighborhoods. ADUs can generate rental income of $1,500 to $3,000 monthly in desirable Chicago neighborhoods.

### Custom Home Building in Chicago

Custom home building and tear-down-rebuild projects allow Chicago homeowners to create purpose-built residences on existing lots. This approach is common in established neighborhoods like Lincoln Park, Lakeview, and North Center where lot sizes permit new construction but existing homes don't meet modern expectations. Custom home costs in Chicago range from $200 to $400+ per square foot depending on design complexity and finishes. The typical custom home timeline is 12-18 months from design through move-in. Homescape manages all aspects of new construction including architectural coordination, permit expediting, construction management, and punch list completion.

---

## Chicago Permit Information

### Do I Need a Permit for Remodeling in Chicago?

Most residential remodeling projects in Chicago require building permits from the Chicago Department of Buildings (DOB). Projects requiring permits include: kitchen remodels with plumbing or electrical changes, bathroom renovations with plumbing modifications, basement finishing, any structural work, window or door replacements changing opening sizes, electrical panel upgrades, HVAC system replacements, and all additions or new construction.

### How to Get a Building Permit in Chicago

Chicago building permits are obtained through the Department of Buildings. The process involves: submitting architectural drawings (for structural work), paying permit fees, scheduling inspections, and obtaining final signoff. Standard permits typically take 2-4 weeks for approval. Large projects or those requiring zoning review may take longer. Homescape handles the entire permit process for clients, from application submission through final inspection coordination.

### Chicago Permit Fees

Chicago permit fees are calculated based on project value. The base fee structure includes a plan review fee and an inspection fee. For a typical $50,000 kitchen remodel, total permit fees typically range from $500 to $1,500. Permit fees for larger projects like additions or new construction can exceed $5,000.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the average cost of a kitchen remodel in Chicago?

A mid-range kitchen remodel in Chicago typically costs $35,000 to $75,000, according to 2024-2025 market data. This price range includes stock or semi-custom cabinetry, mid-grade countertops like quartz or granite, new flooring, updated lighting, plumbing fixture replacement, and professional labor. Budget kitchen updates (cosmetic only) can run $15,000 to $25,000. High-end kitchen renovations with custom cabinetry, premium appliances, and designer finishes frequently exceed $100,000. Key cost factors include kitchen size, cabinet quality, countertop material, appliance tier, and whether plumbing or walls are relocated.

### How long does a kitchen remodel take in Chicago?

A full kitchen remodel in Chicago typically takes 8-12 weeks from demolition to completion. The timeline breaks down as follows: permit approval (2-4 weeks), demolition and rough work (1-2 weeks), electrical and plumbing rough-in (1 week), drywall and painting (1-2 weeks), cabinet installation (1 week), countertop templating and installation (2 weeks), finish work and appliances (1 week). Factors that extend timelines include permit delays, custom cabinet lead times (8-12 weeks for custom), material backorders, and scope changes during construction.

### Do I need a permit for a bathroom remodel in Chicago?

Yes, most bathroom remodels in Chicago require permits from the Chicago Department of Buildings. Specifically, permits are required when: relocating plumbing fixtures, adding or modifying electrical circuits, changing structural elements, or installing new ventilation. A cosmetic-only bathroom update (new tile, paint, vanity in same location with same plumbing) may not require permits, but any plumbing or electrical work triggers permit requirements. Permit fees for bathroom remodels typically range from $200 to $500. Inspections are required for rough plumbing, rough electrical, and final completion.

### What is an ADU and can I build one in Chicago?

An ADU (Accessory Dwelling Unit) is a secondary residential unit on a single-family lot. Chicago legalized ADUs citywide with the 2020 ordinance, effective May 2021. Chicago now permits three ADU types: coach houses (detached units, often above garages), converted garages, and basement apartments. Requirements include: minimum lot size varies by zone, owner must occupy either main house or ADU, one parking space typically required. ADUs can range from 400 to 1,000+ square feet. Construction costs run $150,000 to $350,000. ADUs can generate $1,500 to $3,000+ monthly rental income in desirable Chicago neighborhoods, making them attractive for homeowners seeking additional income or multi-generational living arrangements.

### How much does basement finishing cost in Chicago?

Basement finishing in Chicago typically costs $25,000 to $60,000 for a standard project, with costs varying by size and amenities. Per-square-foot costs range from $30 to $75. A basic finish (drywall, flooring, basic lighting) runs lower, while a full build-out with bathroom, wet bar, or bedroom adds $15,000 to $30,000. Chicago-specific considerations include waterproofing (essential given clay soil and water table), egress windows (required for bedrooms), and ceiling height requirements. Most Chicago basements have 7-8 foot ceilings, meeting code minimums. Permits are required for all basement finishing projects, with inspections for framing, electrical, plumbing, and final occupancy.

### What Chicago neighborhoods does Homescape serve?

Homescape Construction primarily serves Chicago's North Side and Northwest Side neighborhoods, plus select north and west suburbs. Primary service areas include Lincoln Park, Lakeview, Logan Square, Wicker Park, Bucktown, Lincoln Square, and Andersonville. The company also serves Oak Park, Evanston, Skokie, Park Ridge, and other nearby suburbs. This focused service area allows Homescape to maintain deep knowledge of local building codes, neighborhood architectural styles, and efficient project management with minimal travel time between job sites.
